21514-gryll-grange.title: Gryll Grange
21514-gryll-grange.creator: Thomas Love Peacock
21514-gryll-grange.description: A book by Thomas Love Peacock. Opinion governs all mankind,  Like the blind leading of the blind:--  And like the world, men's jobbemoles  Turn round upon their ears the poles,  And what they're confidently told  By no sense else can be controll'd.

41297-local-color.title: Local Color
41297-local-color.creator: George H. Doran Company
41297-local-color.description: A book by George H. Doran Company. e was not a famous author or even a popular one; he was merely well known as a writer of tales dealing in the main with crime and criminals and criminology. People that liked his writings said he was a realist, who gave promise of bigger things. People that did not like his writings said he was a half-baked socialist.

44755-eighteen-months-imprisonment.creator: D—  S—
44755-eighteen-months-imprisonment.description: A book by D—  S—. ON a dreary afternoon in November, cheerless and foggy as befitted the occasion, and accompanied by that gentle rain which we are told “falleth on the just and on the unjust,” I suddenly, though hardly unexpectedly, found myself in the hands of the law, as represented by a burly policeman in a waterproof cape and a strong Somersetshire accent. The circumstances that led up to this momentous change can be briefly described.

50661-dave-dawson-at-singapore.title: Dave Dawson At Singapore
50661-dave-dawson-at-singapore.creator: Unknown
50661-dave-dawson-at-singapore.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "You take it," Dawson interrupted. "Matter of fact, it was your idea in the first place. There we were, nicely settled in good old England, and what do you do but up and get itchy wings. And so here we are, three weeks later, practically over on the other side of the world. You sure do like to get around, I'll say!"

arxiv-2202-12727.title: Sensorless wavefront correction in two-photon microscopy across different turbidity scales
arxiv-2202-12727.creator: Maximilian Sohmen, Molly A. May, Nicolas Barré, Monika Ritsch-Marte, Alexander Jesacher
arxiv-2202-12727.description: Abstract Adaptive optics (AO) is a powerful tool to increase the imaging depth of multiphoton scanning microscopes. For highly scattering tissues, sensorless wavefront correction techniques exhibit robust performance and present a straight-forward implementation of AO. However, for many applications such as live-tissue imaging, the speed of aberration correction remains a critical bottleneck.

arxiv-2210-12951.title: Distances between fixed-point sets in 2 2 -dimensional Euclidean buildings are realised Thanks: The second author is supported by the New Zealand Marsden fund grant MFP-UOA2122. This research of the third author is supported by ARC grant DP180102437.
arxiv-2210-12951.creator: Harris Leung, Jeroen Schillewaert and Anne Thomas
arxiv-2210-12951.description: Abstract . We prove that if two finitely generated groups act on a metrically complete 2 2 -dimensional Euclidean building, then the distance between their fixed-point sets is realised. Our proof uses the geometry of Euclidean buildings, which we view as CAT ⁡ ( 0 ) \operatorname{CAT}(0) spaces, and properties of ultrapowers of Euclidean buildings. 1.

arxiv-2306-01483.title: Emergent trion-phonon coupling in atomically-reconstructed MoSe 2 -WSe 2 heterobilayers
arxiv-2306-01483.creator: Sebastian Meier, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Matthias Dietl, Philipp Parzefall, Michael Kempf, Johannes Holler, Philipp Nagler, Paulo E. Faria Junior, Jaroslav Fabian, Tobias Korn, Christian Schüller
arxiv-2306-01483.description: Abstract In low-temperature resonant Raman experiments on MoSe 2 -WSe 2 heterobilayers, we identify a hybrid interlayer shear mode (HSM) with an energy, close to the interlayer shear mode (SM) of the heterobilayers, but with a much broader, asymmetric lineshape.

arxiv-2405-15543.title: A tame vs. feral dichotomy for graph classes excluding an induced minor or induced topological minor
arxiv-2405-15543.creator: Martin Milanič, Nevena Pivač
arxiv-2405-15543.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Martin Milanič, Nevena Pivač. A minimal separator in a graph is an inclusion-minimal set of vertices that separates some fixed pair of nonadjacent vertices. A graph class is said to be tame if there exists a polynomial upper bound for the number of minimal separators of every graph in the class, and feral if it contains arbitrarily large graphs with exponentially many minimal separators.

arxiv-2409-18012.title: Number of Eulerian orientations for Benjamini–Schramm convergent graph sequences Thanks: The first author was supported by the Netherlands Organisation of Scientific Research (NWO): VI.Veni.222.303. The second author was supported by the ÚNKP-23-3 New National Excellence Program of the Ministry for

arxiv-2409-18012.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ferenc Bencs, Márton Borbényi, Péter Csikvári. For a graph G G let ε ⁡ ( G ) \varepsilon(G) denote the number of Eulerian orientations, and v ⁡ ( G ) v(G) denote the number of vertices of G G .

arxiv-2411-03055.title: ATM: Improving Model Merging by Alternating Tuning and Merging
arxiv-2411-03055.creator: Luca Zhou*, Daniele Solombrino*, Donato Crisostomi, Maria Sofia Bucarelli, Fabrizio Silvestri, Emanuele Rodolà
arxiv-2411-03055.description: Abstract Model merging has emerged as a cost-efficient approximation to multitask learning. Among merging strategies, task arithmetic ( Ilharco et al., 2022 ) is notable for its simplicity and effectiveness. In this work, we provide a theoretical motivation for task vectors by highlighting that, under single-epoch full-batch gradient descent, they are equivalent to multitask gradients.

arxiv-2506-10133.title: Provable Sim-to-Real Transfer via Offline Domain Randomization
arxiv-2506-10133.creator: Arnaud Fickinger, Abderrahim Bendahi, Stuart Russell
arxiv-2506-10133.description: Abstract Reinforcement-learning agents often struggle when deployed from simulation to the real-world. A dominant strategy for reducing the sim-to-real gap is domain randomization (DR) which trains the policy across many simulators produced by sampling dynamics parameters, but standard DR ignores offline data already available from the real system.

arxiv-2512-18310.title: Color, Sentiment, and Structure: A Comparative Study of Instagram Marketing Across Economies
arxiv-2512-18310.creator: Ritesh Konka, Pranali Kurani
arxiv-2512-18310.description: Abstract Instagram has become a key platform for global food brands to engage diverse audiences through visual storytelling. While previous research emphasizes content-based strategies, this study bridges the gap between content and context by examining how aesthetic elements—such as dominant image colors and caption sentiment—and structural factors like GDP, population, and obesity rates collectively shape consumer engagement.

arxiv-2601-21506.title: IROS : A Dual-Process Architecture for Real-Time VLM-Based Indoor Navigation
arxiv-2601-21506.creator: Joonhee Lee, Hyunseung Shin, JeongGil Ko
arxiv-2601-21506.description: Abstract . Indoor mobile robot navigation requires fast responsiveness and robust semantic understanding, yet existing methods struggle to provide both. Classical geometric approaches such as SLAM offer reliable localization but depend on detailed maps and cannot interpret human-targeted cues (e.g., signs, room numbers) essential for indoor reasoning.

arxiv-2602-18974.title: How Does The Magnetic Gradient Scale Length Influence Complexity of Filamentary Coils in Stellarators?
arxiv-2602-18974.creator: John Kappel, Matt Landreman, Philipp Jurašić, Sophia A Henneberg
arxiv-2602-18974.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by John Kappel, Matt Landreman, Philipp Jurašić, Sophia A Henneberg. The distance between the last closed flux surface (LCFS) and the nearest electromagnetic coils is a dominating factor in the cost, size, and engineering difficulty of stellarators. The smallest magnetic gradient scale length on the LCFS - denoted min ⁡ ( L ∇ 𝐁 ) \mathrm{min}(L_{\nabla\mathbf{B}}) - has been shown to be a good proxy for minimum coil-surface distance in optimizations of a current potential on a winding surface, such as through the REGCOIL method.

arxiv-2603-09490.title: Temporal-Conditioned Normalizing Flows for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2603-09490.creator: David Baumgartner, Helge Langseth, Kenth Engø-Monsen, Heri Ramampiaro

arxiv-2606-04302.creator: Haocheng Xia, Mihir Pamnani, Hanxi Fang, Supawit Chockchowwat, Yongjoo Park

britannica-1911-stilbite.title: Stilbite (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-stilbite.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-stilbite.description: Article 'Stilbite' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. hydrated calcium aluminium silicate, CaAl 2 (SiO 3 ) 6 +6H 2 O. Usually a small proportion of the calcium is replaced by sodium. Crystals are monoclinic, and are invariably twinned, giving rise to complex groups and characteristic sheaf-lide like aggregates. The colour is usually white, sometimes red, and on the perfect cleavage (parallel to the plane of symmetry) the lustre is markedly pearly; hence the name stilbite given by R.

europmc-pmc7231123.title: Evidence that Vitamin D Supplementation Could Reduce Risk of Influenza and COVID-19 Infections and Deaths.

This article reviews the roles of vitamin D in reducing the risk of respiratory tract infections,...

jewish-encyclopedia-1906-asaiah-1874.creator: Morris Jastrow, Jr., Gerson B. Levi

ockham-de-sacramento-altaris-birch-1930.description: Birch's 1930 critical edition and English translation of Ockham's 'De Sacramento Altaris' — the only complete work of William of Ockham available in a public-domain English translation. Latin text with facing English translation; the key source for Ockham's nominalism and eucharistic theology.

pamela-giraud-a-play-in-five-acts.creator: Honoré de Balzac

plos-pone-0010822.creator: Zhichao Jin, Danghui Yu, Luoman Zhang et al.
plos-pone-0010822.description: PLOS ONE research article. High quality clinical research not only requires advanced professional knowledge, but also needs sound study design and correct statistical analyses. The number of clinical research articles published in Chinese medical journals has increased immensely in the past decade, but stu

pmc-11455406.title: 12212 A Rare Case Of Central Precocious Puberty In A Male Infant With Adrenal Hypoplasia Congenita
pmc-11455406.creator: Aikaterini Mastoropoulou, Andrew Harry Lane
pmc-11455406.description: Disclosure: A. Mastoropoulou: None. A.H. Lane: None. Introduction: We describe a male with Adrenal Hypoplasia Congenita (AHC) caused by a novel mutation in NR0B1, who was noted at 9 months of age to have central precocious puberty (CPP). Clinical case: A 3 week-old full-term male presented with hypothermia and lethargy, and a 0.3 kg weight loss since birth.

pmc-11595904.title: The Role of 5-Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors (PDE-5I) in Current Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Treatment: A Narrative Review
pmc-11595904.creator: Konstantinos Stamatiou, Gianpaolo Perletti, Vittorio Magri, Alberto Trinchieri
pmc-11595904.description: Introduction: 5-phosphodiesterase inhibitors (PDE-5I) have been investigated as a treatment for urinary dysfunction for almost a decade. The general perception is that they play a significant role in managing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), particularly those associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

pmc-11700531.title: Phaeohyphomycosis of the Eyelid: A Case Report
pmc-11700531.creator: Suwarna Suman, Arushi Kumar
pmc-11700531.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Phaeohyphomycosis is a fungal infection caused by dematiaceous fungi that presents as a superficial, cutaneous, subcutaneous, or systemic infection. Subcutaneous phaeohyphomycosis is the most common manifestation and presents as a subcutaneous nodule or cystic lesions and abscesses. It usually results from traumatic implantation of the saprophytic fungus from soil and vegetative matter; therefore, the commonest sites of infection are the extremities.

pmc-11725075.title: Targeted inhibition of Gus-expressing Enterococcus faecalis to promote intestinal stem cell and epithelial renovation contributes to the relief of irinotecan chemotoxicity by dehydrodiisoeugenol
pmc-11725075.creator: Ruiyang Gao, Bei Yue, Cheng Lv, Xiaolong Geng, Zhilun Yu, Hao Wang, Beibei Zhang, Fangbin Ai, Ziyi Wang, Donghui Liu, Zhengtao Wang, Kaixian Chen, Wei Dou
pmc-11725075.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Irinotecan (CPT11) chemotherapy-induced diarrhea affects a substantial cancer population due to β-glucuronidase (Gus) converting 10-O-glucuronyl-7-ethyl-10-hydroxycamptothecin (SN38G) to toxic 7-ethyl-10-hydroxycamptothecin (SN38). Existing interventions primarily address inflammation and Gus enzyme inhibition, neglecting epithelial repair and Gus-expressing bacteria. Herein, we discovered that dehydrodiisoeugenol (DDIE), isolated from nutmeg, alleviates CPT11-induced intestinal mucositis alongside a synergistic antitumor effect with CPT11 by improving weight loss, colon shortening, epithelial barrier dysfunction, goblet cells and intestinal stem cells (ISCs) loss, and wound-healing. The anti-mucositis effect of DDIE is gut microbiota-dependent.

pmc-12373952.title: Risk factors of depressive and anxiety symptoms in Chinese adolescent girls: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12373952.creator: Juan Juan, Jiayue Li, Xueyin Wang, Di Gao, Bo Song, Xiaosong Zhang
pmc-12373952.description: Depression and anxiety are common in adolescence girls. This study aims to examine the prevalence and risk factors associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms in Chinese adolescent girls. A cross-sectional study was conducted in six provinces in the eastern, central, and western regions of China. A total of 4,658 adolescence girls aged 10–19 years old was included in this study.

pmc-12399097.title: Safety Culture Evaluation in Sarawak General Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Safety Attitude Questionnaire (SAQ)
pmc-12399097.creator: Alex Ren Jye Kim, Shirin Hui Tan, Irene Khai Yen Kho, Farahfaiza Cuki, Yew Fong Lee, Hie Ung Ngian
pmc-12399097.description: BackgroundPatient safety involves proactive and systematic efforts within healthcare settings to prevent harm to patients during medical care. Globally, healthcare organisations prioritise patient safety as a key factor in quality and safety initiatives.ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the patient safety culture at Sarawak General Hospital (SGH), a tertiary referral hospital in Malaysia.

pmc-12425745.title: The influence of direct transportation to neurosurgical-capable medical centers on the clinical outcomes of patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage in urban area: a two-center retrospective study
pmc-12425745.creator: Zijian Chen, Haibo Li, Zhaodi Liao, Xuexiang Shen, Peizhi Qin, Wei Ji, Yuanrun Zhu
pmc-12425745.description: IntroductionSpontaneous intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide due to its poor clinical outcomes. Recent guidelines recommend transferring to medical centers with neurosurgical capabilities to improve outcomes, but it remains unclear whether centers that do not have such neurosurgical capabilities should be bypassed.

pmc-12439689.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Structured Oral Language Therapy on Expressive Language in Preschool Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
pmc-12439689.creator: Hafsa Shams, Irum Nawaz, Shahid Bashir, Benish Shahzadi, Turki Abualait, Hamid Khan, Syed Ali Hussain, Mubin Mustafa Kiyani
pmc-12439689.description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) comprises multiple mental and behavioural variations that mostly appear in early stage of life and effects persistently to all life. Establishing oral language plays an important role in expressive language, with a strong link to understanding reading and writing of ASD children.

pmc-12508444.title: The plastid cysteine synthase complex regulates ABA biosynthesis and stomatal closure in Arabidopsis
pmc-12508444.creator: Sheng-Kai Sun, Nisar Ahmad, Hannah Callenius, Hala Rajab, Veli Vural Uslu, José Rey Cruz Cruz, Fang-Jie Zhao, Markus Wirtz, Rüdiger Hell
pmc-12508444.description: Global warming intensifies drought and high light stress periods, causing severe water loss and decreased crop yield. The phytohormone abscisic acid (ABA) is the dominant signal governing stomatal closure and water loss. Here, we uncover three signaling axes triggered by soil dehydration and high light stress converging on the dynamic assembly of the cysteine-synthase-complex in chloroplasts (pCSC).

pmc-12523692.title: Role of Autophagy Induced by Pmel17 in the Pathogenesis of Vitiligo
pmc-12523692.creator: Lijun Sun, Jingying Sun, Yangmeng Feng, Longfei Zhu, Huijin Li, Cuixiang Xu, Chunyan Guo
pmc-12523692.description: BackgroundVitiligo is a prevalent depigmentation skin disorder with a complex etiology and incompletely understood pathogenesis. Previous studies have suggested a potential involvement of premelanosome protein 17 (Pmel17) in vitiligo, although the specific mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the association between Pmel17 and vitiligo development, as well as its mechanistic actions.

pmc-12527537.title: Complex temporal dynamics of mental health indicators: A longitudinal network approach perspective
pmc-12527537.creator: Matúš Adamkovič, Benjamin Simsa, Bibiána Jozefiaková, Gabriela Mikulášková, Peter Babinčák, Gabriel Baník, Jaroslava Bočanová, Denisa Fedáková, Klára Kačmariková, Pavol Kačmár, Michal Kentoš, Viktória Majdáková, Lenka Vargová, Ľubica Zibrínová, Ivan Ropovik
pmc-12527537.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlthough mental disorders have long been considered complex dynamic systems, our understanding of the mutual interactions and temporal patterns of their symptoms remains limited.MethodsIn this longitudinal study, we examined the structure and dynamics of four key mental health indicators – depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, and insomnia – in a representative sample of the Slovak population (effective N = 3,874) over 10 waves spanning 3.5 years.

pmc-12551716.title: Crystallization-activated moisture barrier for high-tolerance manufacturing of perovskite solar cells
pmc-12551716.creator: Yabin Ma, Chao Luo, Changling Zhan, Keli Wang, Jiandong He, Peng Gao, Zhuye Bi, Yingzhuang Ma, Qing Zhao
pmc-12551716.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Moisture promotes perovskite crystallization during annealing but only within a narrow humidity range, hindering the stable mass production of perovskite solar cells, especially for formamidinium lead iodide. To overcome this, we integrated a “crystallization-activated moisture barrier” into the perovskite film, which can exist in a liquid state/crystallization phase during the initial annealing to allow moisture to enter and promote crystallization, then migrate upward, and form a dense hydrophobic layer on the film surface to protect the perovskite from high humidity–caused damage.

pmc-12559468.title: Synthesis of the Soft Lewis Superacid Tris(4‐bromo‐2,3,5,6‐tetrafluorophenyl)borane B(C6F4Br)3 via C‒Ag to C‒B Transmetalation
pmc-12559468.creator: Amina L. Moshtaha, Erika M. Peter, Robin Sievers, Tim‐Niclas Streit, Moritz Malischewski
pmc-12559468.description: The Lewis acid tris(4‐bromo‐2,3,5,6‐tetrafluorophenyl)borane B(C6F4Br)3 was synthesized via transmetalation from BBr3 and AgC6F4Br. The latter was prepared from 1,4‐C6F4BrSiMe3 with AgF and crystallized as a toluene solvate [2(AgC6F4Br)4•7.46(toluene)]. The solid‐state structure of free B(C6F4Br)3 and its Lewis base adducts with EtCN, H2O, and POEt3 was determined by single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction.

pmc-12584237.title: Knowledge mapping and bibliometric insights into gene therapy for rare inherited hematologic pathologies: focus on sickle cell disease, hemophilia, and thalassemia
pmc-12584237.creator: Moutaz W Sweileh
pmc-12584237.description: BackgroundInherited hematologic disorders such as sickle cell disease (SCD), thalassemia, and hemophilia are rare but devastating conditions with high morbidity and mortality. Advances in gene therapy have opened curative prospects. The objective of the current study was to provide a comprehensive bibliometric and knowledge-mapping analysis of global research on gene therapy targeting SCD, thalassemia, and hemophilia.

pmc-12589278.title: The effect of parental involvement intervention on quality of life and health outcomes among children and adolescents with chronic illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12589278.creator: Manutsawin Kunthamas, Wanida Jaipaeng, Thatchkorn Klaisuban, Kewalin Pongsuwun, Suebsarn Ruksakulpiwat
pmc-12589278.description: The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence from randomized controlled (RCTs) and quasi-experimental studies evaluating the effects of parental involvement interventions on quality of life and health outcomes among children and adolescents with chronic illness. Two independent reviewers screened studies according to predefined inclusion criteria across six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, and Embase).

pmc-13255921.title: Similar Response Dynamics Represent Opposite Behaviors and Rewards in the Frontal Cortex
pmc-13255921.creator: Pingbo Yin, Susanne Radtke-Schuller, Jonathan B. Fritz, Shihab A. Shamma

pmc-13263955.title: Comorbidity of borderline with antisocial and narcissistic personality disorders: a multimethod study
pmc-13263955.creator: Banafsheh Mohajerin, Parham Mohammadi, Richard Howard
pmc-13263955.description: BackgroundThe construct of borderline personality disorder (BPD) remains contentious, with some arguing that it embraces too much pathology to be of any real value as a clinical diagnosis. Examining BPD’s comorbidity is key to understanding its heterogeneous vs. homogeneous nature.

pmc-13264833.title: Reply to “Letter to the editor: methodological considerations in the benchmarking of AI-based protein–aptamer complex prediction”
pmc-13264833.creator: Jiani Zhao, Kha Tram, Hongbin Yan, Yifeng Li
pmc-13264833.description: We thank MD Kazim Okan Dolu for their interest in our published work and for the opportunity to clarify several points regarding software versioning, benchmark independence, secondary-structure generation, binding-free-energy terminology, and negative-control design. We acknowledge that several descriptions in the original manuscript could be stated more precisely.

pmc-13285748.title: Reinvestigation of the mechanism and selectivity of 1,8-cineole synthase using TerDockin
pmc-13285748.creator: Abhay Potluri, Justin B. Siegel, Dean J. Tantillo
pmc-13285748.description: The mechanism of 1,8-cineole formation in Streptomyces clavuligerus 1,8-cineole synthase was reinvestigated using the TerDockin modeling approach and compared to that in Salvia fruticosa. The results of these simulations provided new data on the binding modes of carbocations, the nature of active site bases, and enantioselectivity.

pmc-13312026.title: Predominantly genetic, intrauterine, and lifestyle aetiologies of type 2 diabetes are associated with distinct clinical presentations and risk of complications: a Danish cross-sectional and follow-up study
pmc-13312026.creator: Aleksander Lühr Hansen, Charlotte Brøns, Leonie Mieke Engelhard, Mette K. Andersen, Jens Steen Nielsen, Peter Vestergaard, Kurt Højlund, Michael Hecht Olsen, Henrik Toft Sørensen, Reimar W. Thomsen, Allan Vaag

pmc-13462161.title: False Friends in Fluorescence – Simple HPLC Evaluation of False Positive Fragment Hits in a DiFMUP Assay for Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase 1B
pmc-13462161.creator: Martin Schwer, Sven R Aldea, Benedikt Masberg, Michael Laemmerhofer, Frank M Boeckler
pmc-13462161.description: PurposeDespite their essential role in the reversible protein phosphorylation cycle governing cellular signaling and pathogenesis, phosphatases are frequently overlooked in drug development compared to protein kinases. Protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) is a prominent therapeutic target due to its crucial role in the etiology of diabetes, obesity, and cancer.

pmc-13490177.title: Sex differences in the pathogenesis of degenerative knee osteoarthritis: a comparative transcriptomics analysis
pmc-13490177.creator: Ayobami S. Ogunsola, Davis J. Brady, Jeffrey A. Foster, Marcel G. Brown, Molly A. Hartzler, Maxwell K. Langfitt, John S. Shields, Xue Ma
pmc-13490177.description: IntroductionOsteoarthritis (OA) is one of the leading diseases worldwide and is expected to continue to rise in prevalence. Epidemiological studies on OA have long shown a sex discrepancy between males and females, with females consistently showing greater rates of OA. There are numerous theories about why this might be the case; however, the discrepancy is still poorly understood.

pmc-13498560.title: Diversity, richness, and species composition of fruit flies with new and first records from Meghalaya, India
pmc-13498560.creator: Kennedy Ningthoujam, K J David, Sunita Chetry, Hissay Cheday Bhutia, Bihari Mohapatra Niladri, Kisan Rymbai, Jyotim Gogoi, Deepika Sorahia, Chada Anu Reddy, Pradeep Kumar Chandra, Mareena Sorokhaibam, Khaba Moirangthem, Mahesh Pathak, Uma Ngangom, Lourembam Sanajaoba, K M Ajaykumara, Bimal Kumar Sah
pmc-13498560.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fruit flies are cosmopolitan insects affecting almost all the fruit growing regions of the world. This insect is of significant economic importance as they can cause serious damage to fruit, sometimes resulting in almost total crop failure. This study investigates the diversity and species composition of fruit flies in relation to host availability with the aim of identifying and recording new species of fruit fly in Meghalaya and across the Indian sub-continent.

pmc-13585183.title: Effects of Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on the Night Before Surgery on Postoperative Delirium in Elderly Patients Undergoing Total Knee/Hip Arthroplasty. A Parallel-Arm, Randomized Controlled, Non-Inferiority Trial
pmc-13585183.creator: Yangyang Chen, Keqin Wang, Yuqi Zhang, Ziqian Zhang, Tianyu Yin, Yucheng Liu, Chi Wang, Weijia Chen, Mengying Zhang, Linlin Zhao, Yan Wu, Xinghe Wang, Su Liu
pmc-13585183.description: ImportanceIt is crucial to identify preoperative treatment methods that can safely and effectively reduce the incidence of postoperative delirium.ObjectiveTo evaluate whether preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine administration for preventing postoperative delirium is non-inferior to intravenous dexmedetomidine infusion on the operative day before induction for elderly patients undergoing elective knee/hip arthroplasty.

pmc-13631039.title: Impression management in distributive justice: balancing fairness and social perception
pmc-13631039.creator: Gahyun Lim, Daeeun Kim, Hackjin Kim
pmc-13631039.description: Distributive justice involves choices between principles such as strict equality and merit-based equity. This study examined whether individuals use these principles strategically to manage impressions, signaling warmth or competence in resource allocation. In Experiment 1, allocation choices differed according to evaluator orientation, although evaluator selections were also linked to monetary incentives.

uslaw-cfr-t10-s708-27.title: 10 C.F.R. § 708.27 — The Administrative Judge may not require that the parties participate in alternative dispute resolution.
uslaw-cfr-t10-s708-27.creator: Department Of Energy
uslaw-cfr-t10-s708-27.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 10 (Energy), Part 708 (Doe Contractor Employee Protection Program). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The Administrative Judge may recommend, but may not require, that the parties attempt to resolve the complaint through alternative dispute resolution. Within 5 days of appointment, the Administrative Judge will make the contact information for the DOE's Alternative Dispute Resolution Office.

uslaw-cfr-t22-s1006-875.title: 22 C.F.R. § 1006.875 — May I ask the debarring official to reconsider a decision to debar me?
uslaw-cfr-t22-s1006-875.creator: Inter-American Foundation
uslaw-cfr-t22-s1006-875.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 22 (Foreign Relations), Part 1006 (Governmentwide Debarment And Suspension (Nonprocurement)). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, as a debarred person you may ask the debarring official to reconsider the debarment decision or to reduce the time period or scope of the debarment. However, you must put your request in writing and support it with documentation.
